title: 为谁的安全？拒绝主题的正确子集而非整个主题
summary: 本文探讨了大型语言模型（LLM）在安全对齐中的粒度问题，指出现有安全机制往往过度拒绝，导致模型对包含敏感子主题的广泛话题完全回避，从而限制了模型的有用性。作者提出一种更精细的安全策略：模型应学会识别并拒绝主题中真正有害的子集，而非整个主题。文章通过具体案例（如医疗建议、政治讨论）展示了过度拒绝的弊端，并介绍了一种基于细粒度分类和上下文感知的训练方法，使模型能够区分安全与不安全的子主题，在保持安全性的同时提升回答的准确性和实用性。该方法涉及数据构建、模型微调及评估，强调在安全与有用性之间取得平衡。作者认为，当前的安全对齐实践过于粗放，需要转向更细致的风险控制，以更好地服务不同用户群体的需求。
summary_en: This article explores the granularity issue in safety alignment of large language models (LLMs), pointing out that existing safety mechanisms often over-refuse, causing models to completely avoid broad topics containing sensitive subtopics, thus limiting their usefulness. The authors propose a finer-grained safety strategy: models should learn to identify and refuse only the truly harmful subset of a topic, rather than the entire topic. Through concrete examples (e.g., medical advice, political discussions), they illustrate the drawbacks of over-refusal and introduce a training method based on fine-grained classification and context awareness, enabling models to distinguish between safe and unsafe subtopics while maintaining safety and improving accuracy and practicality. The approach involves data construction, model fine-tuning, and evaluation, emphasizing a balance between safety and helpfulness. The authors argue that current safety alignment practices are too coarse and need to shift toward more nuanced risk control to better serve diverse user needs.
